presentingComplaint: New fever, productive cough and increasing oxygen requirement on day 6 of a surgical ward admission.
history: Admitted 6 days earlier for open reduction and internal fixation of a fractured femur. From the morning of day 6 he developed rigors, purulent yellow-green sputum and worsening breathlessness. He has NOT been intubated or ventilated at any point. Background: type 2 diabetes, ex-smoker (40 pack-years), reduced mobility since surgery. Received a course of IV cefuroxime perioperatively (within the last 90 days). No recent travel, no aspiration event witnessed.
examination: Alert and oriented but appears unwell and flushed. Reduced air entry with bronchial breathing and coarse crepitations over the right lower zone; dullness to percussion at the right base. No neck stiffness, no calf swelling, no new cardiac murmur. Chest wall and surgical wound clean. Pertinent negatives: no witnessed aspiration, not on a ventilator, no foul-smelling sputum.
imaging: Portable chest radiograph: new right lower zone air-space consolidation with air bronchograms, not present on the admission film. No cavitation, no large effusion.
microbiology: Sputum Gram stain: numerous polymorphs with Gram-negative bacilli; sputum and blood cultures sent, pending. Legionella/pneumococcal urinary antigens sent.
citations: IDSA/ATS Management of Adults with Hospital-Acquired and Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia 2016
stewardship: Empiric IV piperacillin-tazobactam covering Pseudomonas and Gram-negative bacilli plus MSSA; no MRSA or double anti-pseudomonal coverage required as he lacks high mortality risk and has no MRSA risk factors per IDSA/ATS 2016 HAP algorithm. De-escalate on culture results.
contraindications: Penicillin anaphylaxis — substitute cefepime or levofloxacin
Renal impairment — dose-adjust piperacillin-tazobactam to eGFR
Add vancomycin/linezolid only if MRSA colonised or high mortality risk
edgeCases: If patient were ventilated this would be VAP, not HAP, with different empiric thresholds
Pulmonary embolism can mimic HAP in a post-op immobile patient with hypoxia — normal-ish lactate and clear consolidation favour pneumonia but a low threshold for CTPA if consolidation is absent
Prior antibiotic exposure and hospitalisation elevate MDR/Pseudomonas risk
expectedMaiK: New consolidation with fever, purulent sputum and rising oxygen requirement arising >48h into admission indicates hospital-acquired pneumonia; start empiric anti-pseudomonal cover and de-escalate to culture-directed therapy once sensitivities return.
expectedNextQuestions: Has the patient been intubated or mechanically ventilated (to distinguish HAP from VAP)?
Any local antibiogram data or prior MDR/Pseudomonas/MRSA colonisation?
expectedInvestigations: Blood and lower-respiratory (sputum/endotracheal) cultures before antibiotics
Legionella and pneumococcal urinary antigens; consider CTPA if PE not excluded

investigations: Blood and respiratory cultures before antibiotics

regressionAssertions: must not diagnose VAP unless mechanicalVentilation is true
empiric regimen must include anti-pseudomonal beta-lactam
